challenges.name: structured-logs-quiz
challenges.title: What ends up in the log line?
challenges.description: Two snippets from the CodeDev API after the logging fix: a redaction config that looks right, and a debug line on the submit path in production.

questions.explanation: False. pino's redact option takes paths, not key names to look for anywhere: "authorization" matches only a top-level key called authorization. The token sits at req.headers.authorization, so it is written in full. The path has to be spelled out ("req.headers.authorization") or use a wildcard ("*.headers.authorization"); check the pino docs for the path syntax of your version. The safer habit is to not log whole header objects at all: pick the fields you need. The misconception is that a redact list works like a search for a key name at any depth; in pino it does not (the logger you write in this lesson's exercise does, by design), and a test that logs a nested secret is the only way to know which kind you have.

questions.question:
On the submit path of the API, which runs with LOG_LEVEL=info in production:

this.logger.debug(
  { tests: summarizeResults(result.tests), code: submission.code },
  "grading payload",
);

A CPU profile of POST /submissions in production shows summarizeResults at 6% of the handler's time.

Statement: "This line writes nothing in production, yet summarizeResults still runs on every request."
questions.explanation: True. JavaScript evaluates the arguments before it calls logger.debug, so the object literal is built and summarizeResults runs on every request; only then does the disabled debug method return without serializing or writing anything. The profile confirms it. Guard expensive arguments with a level check (if (this.logger.isLevelEnabled("debug")) { ... } in pino) or remove the line. The misconception is that a filtered level is free: filtering saves the serialization and the bytes, not the work you put into the arguments.

challenges.name: structured-json-log-formatter
challenges.title: A JSON logger that joins logs to traces
challenges.description: When a grading job failed on CodeDev, the worker logged "Grading failed for submission" as plain text: no trace id, no submission id, an expired bearer token printed in full, and an Error that came out as {}. Nobody could join that line to the POST /submissions request that failed. Write createLogger(options, bindings = {}), a small pino-style JSON logger used by the API and the worker. logger.log(level, msg, fields?) writes exactly one line with options.write(line): a JSON object (JSON.stringify, no spaces) whose keys come in this order: time (new Date(options.now()).toISOString()), level (the level name), msg, trace_id and span_id (traceId and spanId of options.activeSpan(), read when the line is written; both keys are left out when it returns null), then the remaining fields sorted by key with the default string sort. The remaining fields are the logger's bindings merged with the call's fields, the call's fields winning; fields named time, level, msg, trace_id or span_id are dropped. Rules for every value at any depth (nested objects and arrays; only the top level is sorted, nested keys keep their order): a key whose value is undefined is dropped before merging (so an undefined call field leaves the binding as it was), an undefined array item becomes null; a key that matches an entry of options.redact, compared case-insensitively, gets the value "[REDACTED]" whatever its value was; an Error becomes {"name","message","stack"} where stack is the first frame of error.stack (the first line that starts with "at " once trimmed), and the stack key is left out when there is no such line; a string longer than options.maxStringLength (string length) becomes its first maxStringLength characters followed by "...[truncated]" - msg and the Error's name, message and stack included. Levels are trace 10, debug 20, info 30, warn 40, error 50, fatal 60; a record is written when its level is >= options.level and skipped otherwise. An unknown level, in options.level (when createLogger is called) or in a call, throws new Error("unknown level: <level>"). logger.child(bindings) returns a logger whose bindings are the parent's merged with the new ones (the new ones win, an undefined one is not set), writing through the same options. Input (JSON on stdin): { config: { level, redact, maxStringLength }, steps }. The runner builds options around a fake clock starting at 2026-10-20T09:14:03.000Z and a stack of active spans, replays the steps (advance, enter/exit a span, child, log), and prints every line written, or "!! <message>" when a call throws. In the input, {"$error": {...}} stands for an Error object and {"$undefined": true} for undefined.
hints: Which parts of a line does the logger own and which come from the caller, and in which order do bindings, call fields and the five fixed keys meet? Then: which rules apply to a value no matter how deep it sits?

Look at three places. Where you call options.activeSpan(): inside log, at write time, not when the logger is created. The spread that merges bindings with call fields: the one written last wins. And one recursive function that every value goes through - strings, Errors (check instanceof Error before the plain-object case: an Error's message and stack are not enumerable), arrays and plain objects - where object keys are checked for undefined and for redaction before the value is visited.

A similar record on other data: redact ["apiKey"], maxStringLength 10, level info, no active span, bindings { region: "sg" }, logger.log("info", "cfg", { region: "vn", config: { ApiKey: "k_123", note: "a long note here" }, tags: ["a", undefined] }) at 2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z writes {"time":"2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z","level":"info","msg":"cfg","config":{"ApiKey":"[REDACTED]","note":"a long not...[truncated]"},"region":"vn","tags":["a",null]}. The same call at level debug writes nothing.

tests.name: Lines join the trace: fixed field order, ids from the active span, debug filtered
Child bindings merge with call fields and the call wins; level warn and above
Secrets are redacted at any depth, in arrays and in bindings, whatever the key's case
Errors become name, message and first stack frame, also when nested
